substantive_reconstruction.iff: For fixed c, R_c(A)(i,j)=A(c(j),j) on i=c(j), and0 off that support. Hence off-support-zero implies equality by two cases. Conversely R_c(A)=A forces all off-support A entries to vanish. This is the exact necessary-and-sufficient condition; the source proves its forward direction via that same case split.
substantive_reconstruction.existence: For n>0 choose the unique nonzero row in each nonzero column and row0 for an all-zero column. At-most-one nonzero guarantees off-support zero and therefore equality. Finite choice requires no complexity claim. At n=0 there are no columns, and the empty function exists without selecting an element of an empty set; equality is vacuous.
substantive_reconstruction.fixed_map_counterexample: With n=2,c=id,A=[[0,0],[1,0]], column0 has exactly one nonzero but at row1 rather than c(0)=0. Both sampled amplitudes are0, so reconstruction is the zero matrix. This is a genuine one-sparse input defeating a mismatched fixed map, not existential selection.
substantive_reconstruction.invalid_and_valid_examples: D=[[1,0],[1,0]] cannot be reconstructed for any c because whichever row is chosen for column0 leaves the other1 off support. It is a limitation example outside the one-sparse premise, not its refutation. B=diag(0,3) and c=id reconstructs exactly with amplitudes(0,3); zero-column choice is harmless.
substantive_reconstruction.encoding_boundary: ||B||=3, so entry reconstruction does not make B an alpha1 unitary block. A column support function can be many-to-one and need not be a reversible location oracle. Normalization, amplitude loading, cleanup, access construction and costs remain separate.
